name: Verbier 4 Vallées
locality: Verbier (Val de Bagnes), linked with Nendaz, Veysonnaz, Thyon, La Tzoumaz and Bruson
operator: Téléverbier SA (Verbier sector) with partner lift companies across the 4 Vallées (reference)

source.note: Piste reference data — confirm at source. Approximate Verbier village (Médran lift base)

Search summary: 'situated between the elevations of 1,350 and 3,330 m' (top: Mont Fort). Verbier village is about 1,500 m (reference); the valley gondola base at Le Châble is lower (reference) — confirm. Vertical derived as the difference.

Lift-type breakdown from a search summary of lift listings: 74 lifts including 4 aerial tramways (Jumbo 150 pers., Col des Gentianes 115, Mont-Fort 45, Mont-Gelé 45), 18 gondolas (up to the 30-person Funispace), 20 chairlifts (9 six-seat, 7 four-seat, 1 three-seat, 3 two-seat) and 30 surface lifts (7 T-bars, 23 J-bars). The listed types add up to 72, not 74; another summary gave 68 lifts. 412 km of pistes for the whole 4 Vallées. Uphill capacity and difficulty split not found.
Piste reference data — confirm at source. Ski schools and rental shops operate in Verbier and the other villages; other features not on file

character: Switzerland's largest ski area (412 km on one pass), linking Verbier with Nendaz, Veysonnaz, Thyon, La Tzoumaz and Bruson in Valais. Verbier is known for off-piste and freeride terrain, with Mont Fort (3,330 m) as the high point.
learning: Reference note: each village has ski schools; much of Verbier's own terrain suits intermediate and advanced skiers. Confirm dedicated beginner areas and lesson products.

source.note: Search summary: 'The Verbier area opens on 5 December 2026 and closes on 25 April 2027'

prices.note: CHF 94 at the standard adult rate; from CHF 79 when bought online at least ten days ahead. Youth (born 2002–2011) CHF 80; children (born 2012–2019) CHF 47.
